court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court No.4, Mumbai, A- No.630 of 2014
case_name: Roma Rajesh Tiwari vs Rajesh Dinanath Tiwari
facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife's marriage with respondent-husband was solemnized on 27th April 2009. She has a daughter 'Aarna' born out of wedlock and is seeking interim maintenance as she has no source of income to maintain herself and her daughter.

legal_principles.principle: The right of a wife for maintenance is an incident of the status or estate of matrimony.
legal_principles.held: That the Family Court had proceeded on an erroneous assumption that the wife was not entitled to interim alimony because the husband had sued for nullity of marriage.
cited_cases: Sushila Viresh Chhadva Vs. Viresh Nagshi Chhadva, (1996) 1 Mh.L.J. 288

legal_principles.principle: An order for maintenance pendente lite and costs of the proceedings can be made in any proceeding under the Act.
legal_principles.held: When a fact of marriage is acknowledged or proved alimony follows subject of course to the discretion of the Court in the matter having regard to the means of the parties
cited_cases: Sushila Viresh Chhadva Vs. Viresh Nagshi Chhadva, (1996) 1 Mh.L.J. 288

legal_principles.principle: The Trial Court cannot postpone its decision on the application for interim maintenance and costs till the disposal of the main issue in the substantive matter.
legal_principles.held: The very purpose of an order under Section 24 would be frustrated if the matter of granting interim maintenance and of providing the requisite expenses for the conduct of the proceedings itself is deferred till the final stage of the proceeding
cited_cases: Sushila Viresh Chhadva Vs. Viresh Nagshi Chhadva, (1996) 1 Mh.L.J. 288

outcome.final_order: Rule made returnable forthwith. Respondent bound to bear expenses of maintenance of the Petitioner and their daughter.
